title: NGINX
subtitle: An event-driven server for HTTP, TCP streams, caching and reverse proxying.

tiles.label: HTTP context
tiles.says: NGINX listens on HTTP and serves virtual hosts.
tiles.detail: The http block defines servers bound to ports and names. One event-driven worker handles thousands of connections, keeping hardware costs low.

tiles.label: Stream context
tiles.says: NGINX listens on stream and proxies raw TCP and UDP.
tiles.detail: The stream block balances databases, DNS and other non-HTTP protocols with the same upstream logic, so one tool covers many edges.

tiles.label: TLS termination
tiles.says: NGINX terminates TLS and enforces modern protocols.
tiles.detail: Certificates, ciphers and HTTP/2 are configured once at the edge. Applications behind it stay simple and security audits stay short.

tiles.label: Server blocks
tiles.says: Server blocks match the Host header and port.
tiles.detail: server_name selects the virtual host, so many sites share one address. Consolidation reduces infrastructure and certificate sprawl.

tiles.label: Location rules
tiles.says: Location blocks map URI paths to handlers.
tiles.detail: Prefix, exact and regex matches pick static files, proxies or redirects. Precise routing lets one entry point front many applications.

tiles.label: Upstream groups
tiles.says: Upstream groups name backend servers and balance them.
tiles.detail: Round robin, least connections and hashing distribute requests. Adding capacity is an edit to one block, not an application change.

tiles.label: Passive health
tiles.says: NGINX marks failing servers down and retries elsewhere.
tiles.detail: max_fails and fail_timeout remove broken backends automatically. Users see fewer errors during partial outages.

tiles.label: Keepalive
tiles.detail: Persistent connections cut TCP and TLS handshakes to backends, lowering latency and CPU under sustained load.

tiles.label: Timeouts & limits
tiles.says: Timeouts and limits shield backends from abuse.
tiles.detail: limit_req and limit_conn throttle clients; proxy timeouts stop slow requests from piling up. Capacity is protected before it is exhausted.

tiles.label: Proxy cache
tiles.says: NGINX caches responses and serves them without the backend.
tiles.detail: proxy_cache stores objects on disk with validity rules, cutting origin load and page latency.

tiles.label: Static files
tiles.says: NGINX serves static files with sendfile.
tiles.detail: Kernel-assisted file transfer and compression deliver assets efficiently with minimal CPU.

tiles.label: Reverse proxy
tiles.says: NGINX proxies requests and sets forwarding headers.
tiles.detail: proxy_pass forwards traffic to applications and preserves client details, hiding internal topology from the internet.
